newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - A tale of two states.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-AUSTRALIA SEMIS - A tale of two states.

text.p: TCV NSW T-CORP QTC
SAFA WATC TASCOR
*The spotlight for semi-government bond market was firmly set on two states last week, Queensland and Victoria, with both releasing their 1996/97 budgets.
The spotlight for semi-government bond market was firmly set on two states last week, Queensland and Victoria, with both releasing their 1996/97 budgets.

The Victorian government set a 1996/97 underlying budget deficit of A$700,000, substantially below the estimated A$14.0 million unveiled four months ago in its May economic statement, which was due to the factoring of privatisation receipts.

"The outlook is for a broadly balanced underlying budget position in 1996/97 and further reductions in the net-debt-to-GSP ratio for the remainder of the decade," said David Bassanese, senior economist at BT Australia.
"This should keep Victoria firmly in line for a restoration of its Aaa credit rating in comming years," Bassanese added.
The state went one step towards that goal one day after the budget with Standard & Poor's upgrading its long-term local currency debt rating to AA-plus from AA.
S&P said the new rating reflected the significant reduction in the state's debt, the strong position of the government's finances and the state's broad economic base.
However, traders said the rating move had been more than factored in with Treasury Corp of Victoria (TCV) stock already trading like triple-A rated paper.

Meanwhile, TCV is consolidating its July 2000 bonds into its outstandings hot stocks, and depending on its success, it hopes to establish a new benchmark line of August 15, 2008 stock, carrying a 7.50 percent coupon, by the end of the year.
The restructuring process starts on September 17 and will replace the last of TCV's monthly tenders before its goes to two tenders a quarter.
In Queensland, the new coalition government forecast an underlying budget surplus of A$7.6 million for 1996/97 after a A$180.4 million deficit in 1995/96.

"Overall, in view of Queenland's relatively strong fiscal position, a government would have to do a lot wrong to threaten the current Aaa rating. There is not a lot wrong with this budget," said BT's Bassanese.
Although, it is a "big spending" budget, the increase in spending has been financed by tax increases, he added.

Meanwhile, Queensland Treasury Corp, the state's funding arm, is approaching its tender period having last tapped the market on August 16, but is likely to wait until the Australian Treasury's T-bond tender is out of the way.
The Treasury is offering two tranches of stock amounting to A$700 million on Tuesday.

Semis market otherwise got off to a slow start to the week, mirroring a rally if Treasury bonds after a strong performance in U.S. bonds on Friday, and being largely overshadowed by the futures rollover of stock to December from September contracts, which expired at midday, traders said.
